explore_lenses.label: Why did the rescue take so long?
explore_lenses.title: Deep debris made extraction hazardous
explore_lenses.summary: The reported 10-hour gap between locating Daniela Largo Sánchez and freeing her reflects the risks of moving through unstable collapsed material, not simply a delay in finding her.

claims.text: Bogotá firefighters said crews located Largo Sánchez about 10 hours before her rescue but could not immediately extract her because she was buried too deeply.
Firefighters said they worked carefully through the debris to reach her without causing another collapse, illustrating the tradeoff between speed and rescuer/survivor safety.
Aid agencies regard the first 48 to 72 hours after a collapse as especially important for finding people alive, although survival can extend beyond that when trapped people have food and water.

explore_lenses.title: Aid and recovery operations are expanding
explore_lenses.summary: Authorities are pairing the immediate search with emergency financing and outside assistance, while humanitarian organizations say the earthquake has compounded needs in areas already affected by displacement and armed conflict.

claims.text: The government declared an emergency to speed funding for recovery after initial assessments found roughly 1,600 damaged buildings, including at least 61 that had completely collapsed.
Giovanni Rizzo, Colombia director for the Norwegian Refugee Council, said the quake compounds an already severe humanitarian situation and requires greater support for the response.

María José Torres, the U.N. resident coordinator in Colombia, said aid organizations already operating in conflict-affected areas, including Chocó near the epicenter, have increased capacity to be present with affected communities.
The United States offered more than $15 million in assistance, while Mexico and El Salvador said they planned to send personnel, supplies or aid shipments.

highlights.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is grappling with a significant resurgence of Ebola, having recorded nearly 4,000 confirmed cases and over 1,800 deaths. This outbreak, attributed to the Bundibugyo virus, is now the second-largest Ebola outbreak in history and the fastest-spreading in the country's records.

highlights.title: Ebola Outbreak in Congo Claims Over 2,000 Lives, Marked as Fastest Growing on Record
highlights.summary: The Democratic Republic of the Congo reports that at least 2,000 people have died in its ongoing Ebola outbreak, which is now recognized as the fastest growing on record. As of the latest updates, there have been 4,381 confirmed cases across five provinces. The outbreak reportedly began months before it was officially declared in May, complicating response efforts due to factors such as rebel conflict and infrastructure challenges.

items.title: Rescue Teams Save Woman After 36 Hours Trapped in Colombia Earthquake Rubble
items.text: A 32-year-old woman was rescued alive after being trapped for 36 hours under the rubble of a collapsed building in Pereira, Colombia, following a 7.4-magnitude earthquake. Rescuers located her 10 hours before successfully reaching her, as they continue to search for more survivors amid the devastation.

items.title: David Crowley Wins Wisconsin Democratic Primary, Set to Face Tom Tiffany
items.text: David Crowley, the Milwaukee County executive, has won the Democratic primary for Wisconsin governor, defeating progressive candidate Francesca Hong. Crowley, who was backed by Governor Tony Evers, will face Republican Representative Tom Tiffany in the upcoming November election. This victory marks a notable shift in the Democratic primary landscape, as Crowley represents a more moderate stance compared to Hong's democratic socialist platform.

items.title: Bashar al-Assad Sentenced to Death in Absentia for War Crimes
items.text: A Syrian court has sentenced former president Bashar al-Assad and his brother Maher to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity related to the civil war. The court's decision comes after both men were found responsible for their actions in the conflict, which has resulted in approximately 500,000 deaths. The two brothers are currently believed to be in Moscow. Earlier context: on 2026-08-11, Muninn tracked Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad to Death in Absentia for War Crimes.
